testing.summary: No new/changed test files, per the deliberate human decision recorded in the gate (D4) -- not treated as a defect. Existing suite passes unchanged (61 passed, 0 failed) in the project's own Docker test container. The only non-deletion lines in the diff are the 5 quoted return annotations, all inside files the test run reports at 100% statement coverage (enum.py, settings.py, health_output.py); diff coverage for those lines is therefore 100%, well above the 90% gate. The diff-cover CLI itself could not be executed against this working-tree diff inside the sandbox (the test image has no git binary, and ad hoc bind-mounting the full repo into the image for a one-off diff-cover run was unreliable in this Windows/Docker Desktop sandbox); coverage was instead measured by cross-referencing the actual coverage.xml line-coverage data against every added/modified line in the actual diff (all other diff lines are pure deletions, which do not count toward diff coverage). See coverage block for detail.

warnings.title: Developer's reported file count does not match the actual diff
warnings.detail: The Developer reported '24 files under src/' in their verification summary. The actual diff touches 23 files under src/ (confirmed by `git diff --name-only` filtered to src/), matching the plan's own inventory (1 root + 23 src + 3 docs = 27). The overall total of 27 .py files is correct and no file was missed or edited unnecessarily, but the Developer's own breakdown was off by one, which could mislead a reader cross-checking the report against the plan.
warnings.suggested_fix: Correct the Developer's verification note to '23 files under src/' to match the actual diff and the plan's inventory table.

warnings.title: Running `ruff check .` unscoped inside the test container explodes on .venv and on a pre-existing EXE002 condition
warnings.detail: Running the plan's documented command verbatim as `ruff check . --exclude alembic/env.py` inside the Docker test image produces ~165k errors, because passing `--exclude` on the CLI replaces Ruff's built-in default excludes (which include .venv) instead of adding to them -- so .venv's own third-party source gets linted. Separately, scoping to project paths (src, gunicorn.conf.py) still reports EXE002 (file executable, no shebang) on literally every single .py file under src/ and gunicorn.conf.py, with no correlation to this diff's edits (git shows 100644/non-executable mode for all of them on the host; the image evidently sets the whole src/ tree executable at build/COPY time). The Developer's choice to scope paths explicitly and add --ignore EXE002, attributing it to a Windows/build-permissions artifact, is consistent with what I independently reproduced and is acceptable -- this is a pre-existing, diff-unrelated condition, not introduced by this change.
warnings.suggested_fix: File a separate, out-of-scope ticket to fix the ruff-on-.venv pitfall (use --extend-exclude instead of --exclude in the documented verification command and in CI) and to stop the Docker build from marking src/*.py executable.

recommendations.title: Document the --extend-exclude vs --exclude Ruff pitfall in the testing skill
recommendations.detail: The testing skill's documented lint command (`ruff check . --exclude alembic/env.py`) silently disables Ruff's default .venv exclusion when run from a directory that contains .venv (as the project's own Docker test image does). Switching the documented command to `--extend-exclude` would prevent a future verifier from reproducing the ~165k-error explosion seen during this review.

verdict.summary: A clean, minimal, mechanical removal of `from __future__ import annotations` from all 27 .py files plus a correctly placed, clearly worded prohibition rule in the Python skill. All 5 self-referencing annotations are quoted correctly as whole expressions, no other annotation fails under eager evaluation (verified by importing all 48 src modules and running the full 61-test suite unchanged), and no unrelated edits were introduced. Two minor, non-blocking warnings: a one-file discrepancy in the Developer's own file-count report, and a pre-existing, diff-unrelated EXE002/ruff-exclude environment quirk that the Developer handled reasonably.
